items.title: a `dyn Named<str>` over the SUPERTRAIT `Shape<str>`, on a type implementing `Shape` at two instantiations, answers `area` from `Shape<i32>`'s table on JS (prints `4` where `big` is right); natively rustc refuses the emitted program (E0308)
items.body: Repro: `trait Shape<T> { fun area(self): T; } trait Named<T> with Shape<T> {} struct Square { side: i32 } impl Square with Shape<i32> { .. side * side } impl Square with Shape<str> { .. "big" } impl Square with Named<str> {}` then `let titled: dyn Named<str> = Square { side = 2 }; print(titled.area());` — on 0.43.0 too, outside any bound. B436/B437's per-application tables, one level up the supertrait chain: the object's table for `Named<str>` must take the supertrait's members at the arguments the chain passes (`Shape<str>`). Sizing S–M; solver/transformer + native.

items.kind: bug (solver; false refusal / silent first-provider pick; M)
items.title: a type implementing a bound's trait at TWO instantiations binds the callee's `T` from the FIRST provider and ignores the call's expectation: `let s: str = measure(Square { side = 2 })` with `measure<T, S: Shape<T>>` and `Square: Shape<i32> + Shape<str>` is refused "Expected str, but got i32"; with no expectation it silently picks `i32`
items.body: `derive_generics_from_bounds` asks `trait_args_for_pattern`, which falls back to the first agreeing provider when the maxima do not rank. Rec: an unranked pair binds nothing there, so the expectation (`bind_callee_own_generics_from_expectation`) decides; a call nothing decides is refused as ambiguous, naming both instantiations. The trait-object half (B502) is fixed. Sizing M; solver.

items.kind: bug (analyzer; false refusal; S–M) — B465's family
items.title: a closure LITERAL whose position's closure type takes a `&mut` is refused "cannot mutate immutable 'list'" at three positions B465 does not cover: a RETURN (`fun make(): \|&mut List<i32>\| void { \|list\| list.push(9) }`), a generic parameter instantiated with the closure type (`edits.push(\|list\| list.push(7))` on `List<\|&mut List<i32>\| void>`), and an annotated binding that is never called (`let single: \|&mut List<i32>\| void = \|list\| ..` — "never given a type")
items.body: B465 (R-c) made a literal at a parameter, a struct field and an annotated binding take view parameters whether it writes `&` or not; writing `|&mut list|` works at all three positions here, so these are the positions the rule does not yet reach. Sizing S–M; solver.

items.title: `*{ &m }` (a deref of a block whose tail is a view of a scalar) is refused by rustc natively — E0614 "type `i32` cannot be dereferenced" (the block emits `m.clone()`, then the `*`)
items.discussion: solver-a-46 (Order 46), met building B514's native pin; sweeps/order46/REPORT-solver-a-46.md
items.body: On 0.43.0 as well. `*if c { &a } else { &b }` and `*match ..` build natively; the block tail is the one form that does not. JS reads the value since B514. Sizing S; native.

items.title: a value `if`/`match` choosing between two VIEWS cannot initialize a view binding — `let v = if c { &mut a } else { &mut b }; v.x = 10` is refused since B512 (B496's sentence at each leaf); Rust's equivalent is ordinary
items.discussion: solver-a-46 (Order 46), B512's ruling took the refusal door; sweeps/order46/REPORT-solver-a-46.md
items.body: B512's rec offered two doors: a conditional of views is a view initializer, or refuse with B496's sentence. The refusal shipped (sound, small). The other door needs the binding rooted at every leaf's place for the borrow and liveness checks, `view_binding_mutability` and `compute_view_bindings` to look through branches, and both emitters to bind the chosen pair/reference. Paper: is it wanted, and at what cost.

items.title: B515's v0.45.0 half: the trait-not-in-scope WARNING becomes a refusal — first migrate the estate's own 32 sites (the corpus's 5 in `delta-law.vl`, `number-math.vl`, `time.vl`; the docs' 27 in runnable fences), apply kolt's patch, and give the warning its quick fix (insert the import it names; editor)
items.body: Order 46 shipped door (b): `check_trait_method_scope` warns. The flip is the same pass pushing a diagnostic. Most docs sites are `Iterator` defaults (`filter`, `map`, `to_list`, `fold`…) and pipe sealers (`memo` is `CollPipe`'s / `SetPipe`'s) — worth an owner look at whether those traits belong in the base prelude before the flip, since every iterator chain otherwise needs `import std::iterator::Iterator;`. Sizing S (+ the docs sweep).
